body:
# Independent audit: forced-contact support compression

Full source audited:
`candidate 4bf40258fc44a4e6`.

**PASS, no correction needed.**

- Projection onto the fixed-matrix feasible polyhedron is continuous
  even without a Slater point. A minimal nonnegative normal-cone
  representation uses independent active rows, producing one of
  finitely many linear formulas. Feasibility and nonnegative KKT
  multipliers pass through every fixed-formula subsequence.
- The projection growth bound follows from nonexpansiveness with
  the zero target. The positive dense-target weights have summable
  weighted target norms, so their projection average converges
  uniformly in the continuous normal. Its contact slack is the sum
  of nonnegative slacks with EVERY coefficient positive. Density of
  targets removes every nonforced contact, simultaneously for each
  normal; this does not require a uniform index of removal.
- In the forced-constraint LP, maximizing v_z.A under VA>=c has dual
  equations sum t_w v_w=-v_z and sum t_w c_w=-c_z when its value is
  c_z. These signs are correct. Adding the unit coefficient at z
  gives exactly a positive anchored zero-gap representation. The
  reverse implication averages actual nonnegative slacks. Decomposing
  a zero-gap representation into extreme barycentric representations
  preserves zero gaps and a positive occurrence of z in some extreme.
- Forced normal sets are finite unions of closed tight-gap sets. The
  selected global cuts therefore have exactly the stated measurable
  contact sets. Applying the already proved radial theorem gives
  all total/proper/supporting/pure-base responses, including d1.
- Increasing finite averaging sets gives decreasing contact sets and
  speeds for the SAME fields. Dominated convergence of the nonnegative
  costs and each cap loss is valid even if the finite slopes have no
  uniform bound. Signed payments need not be monotone, correctly
  retained. Choosing a finite index before the erosion parameter
  avoids an unproved exchange of limits.

The resulting exact slope A_* may be held fixed in
`candidate 4c4db2dc9830c76a`.
That combination convexifies the physical responses of one source on
its forced contact set. Neither theorem proves a positive minimax
value or a parity bound for the contact costs.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
